clue.text: Bust, Rodin's last put in park but vandalised

indicators.note: the sculptor's final letter is placed inside the jumbled letters of the next words
something vandalised is smashed about, so the letters of park and but are wrecked into a new order
only the final letter of the sculptor's name is wanted

explanation.surface: A Rodin statue in a park has been vandalised and broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like the sculpture, Rodin being a sculptor, but it is the definition in its sense of broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone bust has failed financially and cannot pay their debts.

clue.text: Cut in British cricket, perhaps, that's not new

indicators.note: the letter for new is left out

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

explanation.surface: British cricket has been cut, and it is nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the game; here it is the chirping bug. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts is to cut it down the middle.

clue.text: Sign relating to hearing organ in confines of nave

indicators.note: the ear word goes between the two outer letters
the confines are the boundary letters of nave

parts.note: otic is the adjective relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A sign about hearing aids is posted inside the church nave.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a posted sign or announcement giving information.

clue.text: Bit of sun around river? It is an unusual occurrence

indicators.note: the sunbeam word goes round the river and it

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: Sunlight shines round a river, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom seen or found is an uncommon event or thing.

clue.text: Hand over a note touring island being enthusiastic

indicators.note: the hand-over phrase with a and note goes round the island letter

parts.note: to pass on is to hand over
te is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a note while touring an island, full of enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionate about a thing is keen and eager, full of strong feeling.

clue.text: Give out drugs to get higher as an exercise

parts.note: to push is slang for selling illegal drugs
up means higher, raised

explanation.surface: A dealer hands out drugs as a way of getting high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'as an' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, lifting the body from the floor with the arms, is a standard physical workout move.

clue.text: Cook lightly bit of gristle? Such is unlikely to succeed

parts.note: to underdo meat is to cook it lightly

indicators.note: a bit of gristle here is only its first letter

explanation.surface: Undercooked meat with gristle in it is unlikely to win anyone over.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor expected to lose is the one predicted not to win, so it fits.

clue.text: Female attendant established, we hear, measure of animal first

indicators.note: the horse measure comes before the next piece

parts.note: a hand is the unit of four inches used to measure a horse's height

indicators.note: we hear means the word for established is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: made means established or constructed

explanation.surface: A female attendant has been set up to measure an animal first.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a woman servant who waits on a mistress.

clue.text: Finished with strike over one beef

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the ram piece sits above the next one

parts.note: past means over or finished
to ram is to strike hard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is finished with a strike over a single beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a complaint; it is the meat. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a spiced smoked cured beef, often served in sandwiches.

clue.text: Swift, perhaps, educational test facing girl getting tense

parts.note: an SAT is a standard school assessment test
Iris is a girl's name
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A student taking an exam sits beside a nervous girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, not the adjective for fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote mocking works such as A Modest Proposal, an example of a lampooning writer.

clue.text: Trouble with greed, say, upset Greek idol

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

indicators.note: in an across clue upset means the word is read backwards

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins, an example of a sin

explanation.surface: Someone is troubled that greed has brought down a Greek idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, is a figure of Greek myth idolised for his looks.

clue.text: Draw back tool initially with trouble — a screwdriver?

parts.note: to cock a gun is to draw back its hammer ready to fire

indicators.note: only the first letter of tool is used

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.walkthrough: A screwdriver is a mixed drink of vodka and orange juice, not the tool the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver, vodka with orange juice, is an example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Place for pilgrims kept by councillor in Norfolk resort

parts.note: Rome is a city Catholic pilgrims visit

explanation.surface: A councillor in a Norfolk seaside town looks after visiting pilgrims.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromer is a seaside town on the north Norfolk coast, known for its pier and crabs.

clue.text: Sickly son fidgeting in each car

clue.text: Moan at sign that's whipped up hostility

clue.text: Assess car that's covered northerly road

clue.text: Computer stuff mistaken for waste

indicators.note: mistaken suggests these letters are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Computer gear has been wrongly binned as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Programs that run on a computer are known collectively by this term.

clue.text: Fine work by engraver that's attractive

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: An engraver's fine work is very pleasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is part of the leaf; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means appealing or charming to look at.

clue.text: Protective garment pierced by dislodged stake in industrial feature

indicators.note: the garment is opened up and the jumbled letters are pushed into it

clue.text: Sixteen, maybe, and uncool

definitions.meaning: sixteen is four times four, an example of a perfect product of a number with itself
conventional and old-fashioned, the slang sense of a stuffy person

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a number multiplied by itself, and a dull conventional person.

clue.text: Note heartless Chancellor of the Exchequer being brutal

parts.note: a fiver is a five-pound banknote

clue.text: Trite characteristic of a fondue?

definitions.meaning: a fondue is melted dairy into which bread is dipped, so it tastes of it

clue.text: Popular diplomat's skill is undiminished

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
tact is the sensitivity a diplomat needs

explanation.surface: A well-liked diplomat's skill remains as strong as ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is not reduced in any way, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Best vehicle leaves without time to go to hotel

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is taken out of the word for leaves

parts.note: quits means leaves or departs
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The best vehicle departs without delay for the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is a verb meaning defeat. 'to go to' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, so it means overcome or defeat.

clue.text: Artist following a writer in foreign language

indicators.note: the artist's letters come after the a

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: An artist works after a writer, in a foreign language.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the language of much of the Middle East and North Africa, foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Conflict rages sadly in exit

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of rages are in a sorry, disordered state

clue.text: Come out from English commercial move ending prematurely

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a merger joins two companies, a business move

explanation.surface: An English company emerges from a business deal that ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or come into view is the meaning shared by both phrases.

clue.text: Measure taken by American in church yard, place of rest

indicators.note: the measure goes inside the church and yard abbreviations

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
meter is the American spelling of the length unit metre

explanation.surface: An American paces out a church graveyard where people lie at rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church yard' reads as one word in the surface but gives CE and Y separately.
